FIGURE 4. Diagnostic analysis on the WIB-100 benchmark. (a) Stratified rejection rates for hard, medium, easy, and temporal-impossible negatives. (b) Effect of the critic penalty factor γ on MCC. (c) Impact of replacing rigid formal connectors with generic prompts.
FIGURE 5. Case studies. (a–b) True positive: Hokusai → Van Gogh. (c–d) True negative: Dalí → Escher, where high visual similarity is overturned by failed pathway evidence and counter-verification.
TABLE IV. Historical constraints that bound the generative agent.

FIGURE 1. Visual summaries of the primary mathematical formalisms in M-ArtAgent. (a) The Observation Formalism (Eq. 1–4): Raw multimodal embeddings are funneled through grammatical projection into an orthogonal 5D Wölfflin manifold W, transforming implicit clustering into explicit formal coordinates. (b) The Adjudication Formalism (Eq. 10): Rather than blindly accepting visual similarity, the ReAct critic subjects the initial confidence c0 to systematic downward pressure from alternative historical hypotheses (H2,H3,H4), actively penalizing and clipping the score to yield a conservative cfinal.

FIGURE 2. M-ArtAgent overview. The framework combines four principal processing layers, with candidate generation integrated into Layer 2, and a four-phase epistemic protocol (Investigation, Corroboration, Falsification, Verdict) that mirrors art-historical scholarship.
